q1: SELECT CLASS FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(*)>=5
q2: WITH AGG AS ( SELECT CLASS , COUNT(*) AS NUMBER FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS) SELECT CLASS FROM AGG WHERE NUMBER >=5
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT CLASS FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(*)>=5
q2_prompt_sql: WITH AGG AS ( SELECT CLASS , COUNT(*) AS NUMBER FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS) SELECT CLASS FROM AGG WHERE NUMBER >=5
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are semantically equivalent. Both queries aim to retrieve classes that have at least 5 courses (i.e., at least 5 distinct students enrolled). Q1 achieves this via HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5 directly in the GROUP BY clause. Q2 uses a common table expression (CTE) to first compute the count per class and then filters using WHERE NUMBER >= 5. Since COUNT(*) on a table with a primary key on STUDENT counts distinct students per class, both queries produce the same result.
